scenario.title: BATTLE OF GRODNO - 20 SEP 1939
intro.text:
BATTLE OF GRODNO - 20 SEP 1939

Southeast of Grodno, East Poland

Move your units across the city of Grodno to the Lithuanian border. Occupy the city and vicinity and break any resistance!

ORDERS
a. Capture all VH!
b. Prevent that more than 2 enemy ground units cross the Polish-Lithuanian border (Exit Points).

CORE (recommended)
2x Tank
4x Infantry (+1)
2x Reconnaissance (+1)
2x Artillery (+1)
1x Fighter Aircraft
1x Tactical Bomber (+1)
header.location: Southeast of Grodno, eastern Poland — 20 September 1939
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.reaction-briliant.text: The Baintsagan attack broke before the Japanese thrusts could support each other. Moscow wants the operation circulated as an example. I've asked that the supply arrangements go with it.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.reaction-victory.text: The river line is secure and the Japanese attack is broken. The staff report isn't finished; the officers still disagree about why it worked.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.reaction-tactical.text: We held the line. There are more damaged vehicles in the repair park than I expected, though. That needs to be settled before another move.
line.callback-choice-a.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.callback-choice-a.text: The young officers keep asking about your drive beyond Baintsagan. I show them the return route as well. They usually stop asking then.
line.callback-choice-b.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.callback-choice-b.text: I'm using your Khalkhin Gol order for the river positions: bring up the guns and supply before moving on. Pavel knows it already.
line.scene-0.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.scene-0.text: This order calls it a frontier march. Our columns are meeting Polish soldiers, militias and refugees in the same villages. Before they move again, they need to know whose instructions apply there.
line.scene-1.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.scene-1.text: I've folded the German liaison overlay underneath ours. It gives the same northern limit, but it tells us nothing about the refugees on the approach roads.
line.decision.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.decision.text: Resistance in Grodno can be bypassed only if the border routes are sealed early. We can lead with mobile groups and risk broken communications, or keep a coherent front and accept that more enemy units may reach Lithuania.
line.decision.choice.seal-the-border.tex: Send the mobile group past Grodno first and close the northern exits.
line.decision.choice.seal-the-border.hin: Give reconnaissance formations 25 experience, fully refuel the core, and gain 60 prestige for sealing the frontier roads.
line.decision.choice.control-the-advance: Clear the approaches in sequence and keep every formation under direct control.
Give infantry 20 experience and artillery 15 experience, and fully replenish ammunition without restoring fuel or strength.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.choice-a-0.text: The mobile group will not become an excuse for indiscriminate fire. It closes roads, reports movement, and leaves the city fight to the forces assigned to it.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.choice-a-1.text: I'll give the detached groups roads and halting points. But once they're among the refugee columns, they will be making decisions we can't supervise. Are we ready for that?
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.choice-b-0.text: Then the advance moves on confirmed orders, not rumour. We may catch fewer columns, but no detached battalion is to invent its own war.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.choice-b-1.text: Have the arrests and shootings recorded under the unit that ordered them. Released prisoners as well. I want to be able to find the officer responsible.
line.post-0.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.post-0.text: Send those reporting instructions to every detachment, including the ones already on the road. I don't want to hear later that nobody received them.
